        - heading "Rust" [level=1] [ref=f209e31]
        - heading "A language empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software." [level=2] [ref=f209e32]
      - generic [ref=f209e33]:
        - link "Get Started" [ref=f209e34] [cursor=pointer]:
          - /url: /learn/get-started

          - link "Version 1.99.1" [ref=f209e36] [cursor=pointer]:

    - generic [ref=f209e38]:
      - heading "Why Rust?" [level=2] [ref=f209e40]
      - generic [ref=f209e42]:
        - generic [ref=f209e43]:
          - heading "Performance" [level=3] [ref=f209e44]
          - paragraph [ref=f209e45]: "Rust is blazingly fast and memory-efficient: with no runtime or garbage collector, it can power performance-critical services, run on embedded devices, and easily integrate with other languages."
        - generic [ref=f209e46]:
          - heading "Reliability" [level=3] [ref=f209e47]
          - paragraph [ref=f209e48]: Rust’s rich type system and ownership model guarantee memory-safety and thread-safety — enabling you to eliminate many classes of bugs at compile-time.
        - generic [ref=f209e49]:
          - heading "Productivity" [level=3] [ref=f209e50]
          - paragraph [ref=f209e51]: Rust has great documentation, a friendly compiler with useful error messages, and top-notch tooling — an integrated package manager and build tool, smart multi-editor support with auto-completion and type inspections, an auto-formatter, and more.
    - generic [ref=f209e53]:
      - heading "Build it in Rust" [level=2] [ref=f209e55]
      - paragraph [ref=f209e58]:
        - text: In 2018, the Rust community decided to improve the programming experience for a few distinct domains (see
        - link "the 2018 roadmap" [ref=f209e59] [cursor=pointer]:
          - /url: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2018/03/12/roadmap.html
        - text: ). For these, you can find many high-quality crates and some awesome guides on how to get started.
      - generic [ref=f209e60]:
        - generic [ref=f209e61]:
          - img "terminal" [ref=f209e63]
          - generic [ref=f209e64]:
            - heading "Command Line" [level=3] [ref=f209e65]
            - paragraph [ref=f209e66]: Whip up a CLI tool quickly with Rust’s robust ecosystem. Rust helps you maintain your app with confidence and distribute it with ease.
            - link "Building Tools" [ref=f209e67] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /what/cli
        - generic [ref=f209e68]:
          - img "gear with puzzle piece elements" [ref=f209e70]
          - generic [ref=f209e71]:
            - heading "WebAssembly" [level=3] [ref=f209e72]
            - paragraph [ref=f209e73]: Use Rust to supercharge your JavaScript, one module at a time. Publish to npm, bundle with webpack, and you’re off to the races.
            - link "Writing Web Apps" [ref=f209e74] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /what/wasm
        - generic [ref=f209e75]:
          - img "a cloud with nodes" [ref=f209e77]
          - generic [ref=f209e78]:
            - heading "Networking" [level=3] [ref=f209e79]
            - paragraph [ref=f209e80]: Predictable performance. Tiny resource footprint. Rock-solid reliability. Rust is great for network services.
            - link "Working On Servers" [ref=f209e81] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /what/networking
        - generic [ref=f209e82]:

            - heading "Embedded" [level=3] [ref=f209e86]
            - paragraph [ref=f209e87]: Targeting low-resource devices? Need low-level control without giving up high-level conveniences? Rust has you covered.
            - link "Starting With Embedded" [ref=f209e88] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /what/embedded
    - generic [ref=f209e90]:
      - heading "Rust in production" [level=2] [ref=f209e92]
      - paragraph [ref=f209e95]:
        - text: Hundreds of companies around the world are using Rust in production today for fast, low-resource, cross-platform solutions.
        - strong [ref=f209e96]: From startups to large corporations, from embedded devices to scalable web services, Rust is a great fit.
